title: Problem 05
markdown:
### Problem
Evaluate

$$\int_2^4 \lfloor x^3 - 6x^2 + 12x - 6 \rfloor \, dx,$$ 

where for every real number $t$, $\lfloor t \rfloor$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$.

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
The value of the integral is $17 - \sum_{n=2}^7 \sqrt[3]{n}$.

Notice that $(x - 2)^3 = x^3 - 6x^2 + 12x - 8$. Therefore:

$$x^3 - 6x^2 + 12x - 6 = (x - 2)^3 + 2.$$

Since 2 is an integer, $\lfloor (x - 2)^3 + 2 \rfloor = \lfloor (x - 2)^3 \rfloor + 2$.

Thus:

$$\int_2^4 \lfloor x^3 - 6x^2 + 12x - 6 \rfloor \, dx = \int_2^4 \lfloor (x - 2)^3 \rfloor \, dx + \int_2^4 2 \, dx = \int_2^4 \lfloor (x - 2)^3 \rfloor \, dx + 4.$$

Make the substitution $u = x - 2$, so $dx = du$, and as $x$ ranges from 2 to 4, $u$ ranges from 0 to 2:

$$\int_0^2 \lfloor u^3 \rfloor \, du.$$

Partition the interval $[0, 2]$ at the points $u = \sqrt[3]{n}$ for $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots, 8$:
- On $[0, 1)$, $\lfloor u^3 \rfloor = 0$, integral $= 0$.
- On $[\sqrt[3]{n}, \sqrt[3]{n+1})$, $\lfloor u^3 \rfloor = n$, with interval length $\sqrt[3]{n+1} - \sqrt[3]{n}$.

Summing the piecewise integrals for $n = 1$ to $7$:

$$\begin{aligned} \int_0^2 \lfloor u^3 \rfloor \, du &= \sum_{n=1}^7 n(\sqrt[3]{n+1} - \sqrt[3]{n}) \\ &= 1(\sqrt[3]{2} - 1) + 2(\sqrt[3]{3} - \sqrt[3]{2}) + \dots + 7(2 - \sqrt[3]{7}) \\ &= 7(2) - 1(1) - \sum_{n=2}^7 \sqrt[3]{n} \\ &= 13 - \sum_{n=2}^7 \sqrt[3]{n}. \end{aligned}$$

Adding back the $+4$ gives:

$$\int_2^4 \lfloor x^3 - 6x^2 + 12x - 6 \rfloor \, dx = 17 - \sum_{n=2}^7 \sqrt[3]{n}.$$

### Conceptual Explanation
Completing the cube yields $(x - 2)^3 + 2$. Substituting $u = x - 2$ shifts the integral to $\int_0^2 \lfloor u^3 \rfloor du + 4$. Summing the stepwise blocks $\sum_{n=1}^7 n(\sqrt[3]{n+1} - \sqrt[3]{n})$ telescopes into $13 - \sum_{n=2}^7 \sqrt[3]{n}$, giving total $17 - \sum_{n=2}^7 \sqrt[3]{n}$.

### Key Technique
Completing the cube $(x-2)^3$ and summation by parts / telescoping on floor integrals.
